items.q: Match each population with its most common cause of RAS — 1) Overall 2) Young population 3) Indian/Asian population … A) Takayasu arteritis B) Atherosclerosis C) Fibromuscular dysplasia
items.exp: Overall: atherosclerosis; young population: fibromuscular dysplasia; Indian/Asian: Takayasu arteritis. (Book p750)

items.q: In young males, the cause of RAS that involves the entire length of the renal artery with microaneurysms is:
items.exp: Young males: polyarteritis nodosa – entire length renal artery – microaneurysm. (Book p750)

items.q: Atherosclerotic RAS involves the proximal renal artery over 1-2 cm and becomes symptomatic beyond what occlusion?
items.exp: Atherosclerosis: proximal renal artery (1-2 cm); symptomatic: >80% occlusion. (Book p750)

items.q: Fill up: Fibromuscular dysplasia, the young-population cause, affects the ______ renal artery.
items.exp: Fibromuscular dysplasia (arteriopathy): mid to distal renal artery. (Book p750)

items.q: The female-to-male ratio written for Takayasu arteritis is:
items.exp: Takayasu arteritis (F:M = 9:1), proximal renal artery. (Book p750)

items.q: The types of RAS are explained by the Goldblatt:
items.exp: Explain by Goldblatt: two kidney one clip model. (Book p750)

items.q: The pathogenesis of unilateral RAS starts with the clue:
items.exp: Unilateral RAS pathogenesis: asymmetric kidney size. (Book p750)
